chunks: Thus, both paths depend on the invalidation of the beliefs of these groups in order that our purpose is established, and they require the establishment of the three principles we mentioned: the necessity of leadership (Imamate), the necessity of certainty regarding political authority), the necessity of certainty regarding infallibility, and that the truth does not depart from the Ummah. We provide evidence for each of these statements with a concise argument, as their full elaboration exists in our book on Imamate to an extent that cannot be exceeded. The purpose of this book is specifically to address the occultation and nothing else, and Allah is the One who grants success in this through His grace.

key_terms.الرِّئَاسَة: Leadership/Imamate (specifically referring to political and spiritual authority)
key_terms.الْعِصْمَة: Infallibility (the quality of being protected from error and sin)
key_terms.الْغَيْبَة: Occultation (the hidden state of the Imam)
key_terms.الْفِرَق: Groups/Sects (referring to various Islamic theological factions)

ai.seo_question: What are the three foundational principles required to establish the doctrine of the Imam's occultation according to Al-Tusi?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi structures his argument by asserting that the validity of the occultation narrative depends on refuting opposing sects and establishing three foundational principles: the necessity of leadership (Ri'asah), the certainty of infallibility (Ismah), and the principle that truth remains within the community (Al-Haqq la yakhruj min al-Ummah). While he references his comprehensive work on Imamate for detailed proofs, this text specifically isolates the occultation as the unique context for these doctrines, emphasizing divine facilitation for the specific theological goal.
